subject: ex-cg-a-tilde-2-nerve-perimeter-two-pi-and-vanishing-gram-determinant
description: Reader-reported F5 cited determinant uniqueness for singularity iff determinant zero. Current exact matrix-invertibility supplier supports the inference.

evidence.note: Read the complete Example, F1–F7 and five Verification steps with all eleven dependency statements. Each 2x2 minor is 3/4>0; r^k and r^k s (0<=k<3) are all normal forms and have six distinct permutation images, giving order six. C_S=(3/2)I-(1/2)J has kernel (1,1,1) and eigenvalue 3/2 on the two-dimensional sum-zero space, so its determinant vanishes and no triangle cell exists. The raw Schur complement has diagonals 3/4; normalization gives entries +/-1. Two genuine link components give distance pi without inventing an edge. The entire nerve is the three-edge circle of circumference 2pi; minimum-of-two-arc distances have diameter pi, so truncation preserves the metric. An isometric smaller circle would give two distinct geodesics at distance <pi, contradicted by uniqueness of the shorter arc. Local computation supports the exact equality; Möller Proposition 3.4 supplies only a non-strict bound, as the repaired locator now says. No general large-flag theorem or AC is required.

subject: ex-cg-all-right-triangle-versus-disconnected-universal-coxeter-nerve
description: Reader supplied the omitted free-product universal-property argument in current 1.2.

evidence.note: Read all seven Verification steps and eleven dependency statements. Commuting involutions have eight exhaustive normal forms with distinct images in (Z/2)^3; the identity Gram matrix realizes the convex positive octant. The universal property proves the free-product identification, and the integer reflection images show every distinct-generator pair is infinite. Truncated distances between point components are pi; equal pairs and constant triangles satisfy CAT(1). The filled octant's diameter <=pi/2 and uniqueness of short great-circle arcs exclude every isometric circle. Corner points at t<pi/4 have cos(distance)=cos^2(t)>cos(2t), giving strict local shortening; no claim is made that all arcs below 2pi minimize. Correct singleton/empty metric flag tests remain, and nonedge pi is not an edge length. Alpha adds the essential continuity qualifier to step 4.1 (an isometric embedding is continuous), since an arbitrary map from a circle to a discrete set need not be constant, and makes off-diagonal quantification explicit in Example (i). The sole direct reference consumer is the assigned examples page, whose filled/discrete comparison remains sound. No AC is consumed.

subject: thm-cg-large-metric-flag-short-loop-radial-contradiction
description: Reader added the essential locally CAT(1) qualification to the title's theorem claim; the Statement already carried it.

evidence.note: Read all four proof steps, all thirteen dependency interfaces and the previously independently reviewed minimum-loop/Bowditch chain. The reduction used is existential for a shortest circle maximizing visits, not universal for every shortest circle. Empty spaces and CAT(1) components are handled before the non-CAT(1) supposition. A simplicial closed edge walk cannot have one edge, a two-edge walk is a backtrack with length-controlled contraction, and four edges cost >=2pi; hence exactly three distinct vertices remain. With a,b,c in [pi/2,pi), b+c>=pi>a gives strict triangle inequalities; s and s-a,s-b,s-c are in (0,pi), including the all-right endpoints. The determinant product is positive and Sylvester applies. Metric flagness fills this exact triple; positive Gram definiteness makes corner angles strictly between 0 and pi. For sufficiently small t with 2t<pi, cos(distance)-cos(2t)=sin^2(t)(1+cos(alpha))>0, so the available spherical shortcut contradicts local geodesicity. No global edge-cell distance equality is assumed except when justified by the chosen isometric circle. AC is inherited through attained short circles; all finite counting and determinant steps are choice-free. Davis I.7.4's final three-circuit argument agrees with this local proof.
